issue.standard_remedy: Route off-contract buying to contracted suppliers
issue.summary: 58% of category spend is off contract

plan.diagnosis: 58% of Copper wire & bar category spend ($31,970,175 of $55,068,810 total) is occurring off-contract across 9 plants in a direct material category, indicating lack of source enforcement and decentralized buying practices. This high maverick spend rate in a strategic direct material suggests either inadequate contract coverage, poor supplier master data governance across the multi-ERP landscape (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa), or buyers bypassing established contracts.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct immediate audit across all 9 plants to identify which suppliers are receiving the $31,970,175 maverick spend and verify whether contracted suppliers can fulfill all plant requirements for copper wire & bar specifications
remedy_steps.owner: Category Manager - Metals & Strategic Sourcing Lead

remedy_steps.step: Implement system-level source restrictions: configure approved vendor lists and source lists in SAP (ME01), Oracle EBS (Approved Supplier Lists), Dynamics 365 (trade agreements), and NetSuite (preferred vendor records) limiting copper wire & bar purchases to contracted suppliers only

Enable requisition-to-PO workflow approvals in Coupa for any copper wire & bar purchases attempting to use non-contracted suppliers, routing to Category Manager for exception approval with business justification
Deliver mandatory training to plant buyers and requestors across all 9 locations on contracted supplier requirements, catalog usage, and escalation process for specification gaps
Establish monthly spend compliance dashboard tracking on-contract vs off-contract copper wire & bar spend by plant and supplier, with plant manager accountability for variance explanations

plan.expected_impact: Redirecting 80% of the $31,970,175 maverick spend to contracted suppliers at negotiated rates should yield $2,557,614 in savings assuming an 8% price variance reduction through volume leverage and contracted pricing.
kpis: Maverick spend % in Copper wire & bar category (target: reduce from 58% to <15% within 90 days)
On-contract spend $ (target: increase from $23,098,635 to $48,000,000+ within 6 months)
Number of active copper wire & bar suppliers (rationalization target based on audit findings)
PO compliance rate by plant (% of copper wire & bar POs using approved source lists)
Average price variance vs. contracted rates for copper wire & bar
risks: Contracted suppliers may lack capacity or specific product specifications required by certain plants, forcing continued maverick purchases
Multi-ERP environment creates master data synchronization challenges and enforcement gaps if source lists are not consistently maintained
Plant resistance to centralized sourcing if historical maverick suppliers provided superior service or technical support
Implementation timeline conflicts if ERP system resources are committed to other priority projects
Contracted supplier delivery failures during transition could disrupt production at the 9 plants
erp_actions: SAP: Create source lists (ME01) for copper wire & bar material groups limiting to contracted suppliers; set purchasing info records (ME11) with contracted pricing; apply vendor blocking indicators (LFB1 posting block) for non-contracted copper suppliers at plant purchasing org level
Oracle EBS: Configure Approved Supplier Lists for copper wire & bar items; update blanket purchase agreements with contracted suppliers; restrict requisition import for non-approved vendors
Dynamics 365: Establish trade agreements for contracted copper suppliers with price enforcement; configure procurement category policies to require approved vendor selection
NetSuite: Mark contracted copper suppliers as Preferred Vendors; configure item records to display only approved suppliers; enable purchase approval workflows for non-preferred vendor usage

Coupa: Update catalogs with contracted supplier copper wire & bar items; configure supplier enablement rules to route requisitions to contracted suppliers; implement approval chains for off-contract requisitions >$5,000
